title: Send
description:
One dispatch of one article to a newsletter's list.

The three counts are a `send.completed` event's three counts under the
same names. `recipient_count` is the audience size fixed at the moment
the run started, which is the stable denominator for any rate.
`sent_count` is what the sending provider accepted at dispatch, which is
**not** a confirmed delivery: confirmations arrive afterwards, one per
recipient, as `delivery.delivered`, and are never counted back into this
shape. `failed_count` is what the provider rejected outright.

**Read `completed_at` before reading either count.** It is null while
the run is still going, and until it is stamped `sent_count` and
`failed_count` are both `0`. They are not a progress report: the
dispatch settles them once, at the end.

**The counts are what the run finished on, and they stay there.** A
later re-attempt of the recipients this run could not reach does not
move them, so this resource never disagrees with the `send.completed`
event that announced it.

**Opens and clicks are not here**, and neither is a `status`. Opens and
clicks come from the sending provider on its own schedule. A run that
broke is reported by the article's own `status`.

id.description:
Stable identifier for the run. The `send_id` on `send.completed`
and on `send.failed` is this value.

article.description:
The article that was dispatched. A `Ref` unless `article` is named in
`?expand=`, and `null` when the article is one this credential may not
read. An article dated in the future is hidden from everybody,
including the newsletter's own team, so its run reports `null` here
rather than a reference whose own operation would answer `404`.

newsletter.description:
The newsletter that sent it. A `Ref` unless `newsletter` is named in
`?expand=`.

started_at.description: When the run began handing recipients to the provider.

completed_at.description:
When the run finished handing every recipient over. Null while it is
still going, and null for a run that broke before it could finish.
The counts below mean nothing until this is set.

recipient_count.description: Audience size fixed at the moment the run started. The stable denominator for any rate a consumer computes.

sent_count.description: Recipients the provider accepted at dispatch. NOT confirmed deliveries: confirmation arrives later as `delivery.delivered`, one event per recipient.

failed_count.description: Recipients the provider rejected outright at dispatch.

created_at.description:
When the run was recorded, which is the same instant as
`started_at` for every run Commune has made. The collection is
ordered by this rather than by `started_at`, which can be absent.

Article.title: Article
Article.description:
One article of a newsletter, without its body. Every collection of
articles returns this shape. `GET /articles/{article}` returns
`ArticleWithContent`, which is this plus `content`.

short_id.description:
Eight character base62 identifier, unique across Commune. Safe in a
URL and accepted anywhere `{article}` is.

slug.description:
URL segment under the newsletter, unique within it but not across
Commune. The permalink is `/n/{handle}/a/{slug}`. Falls back to the
`short_id` for an untitled article.

newsletter.description:
The newsletter this article belongs to. A `Ref` unless `newsletter` is
named in `?expand=`.

title.description: Subject line of the article. Null for an untitled draft.

preview_text.description:
The short line email clients show after the subject, and what
Commune uses as the excerpt on a card.

image_url.description:
Cover image. When the creator set none, Commune stamps the first
image in the body at send time, so this is usually populated for a
sent article.

external_url.description:
The article's canonical URL on the newsletter's own provider, for an
imported article. Null for one written in Commune.

is_imported.description:
`true` when the article came in from the newsletter's provider,
`false` when it was written and sent in Commune.

posted_at.description:
When the article went out. An article dated in the future is not
returned by any read operation until that moment passes, so this is
never ahead of now in a response.

scheduled_for.description:
When a queued article may go out. Set while `status` is `scheduled`
and null otherwise.

This is not `posted_at` and the difference matters: a queued article
has no publication date yet, which is why it stays invisible on
every reader surface until it really goes out. Commune dispatches
in passes, so this is the moment from which the article may go rather
than the moment it will.

authors.description:
The byline, in order. Each entry is a `Ref` unless `authors` is
named in `?expand=`. Empty when no Commune account is credited.

thread.description:
The chat thread this article opened, where its discussion lives.
`null` when the newsletter does not open a thread per article. A `Ref`
unless `thread` is named in `?expand=`.

created_at.description: When the row was created in Commune.

updated_at.description: When the article was last edited.

ArticleStats.title: ArticleStats
ArticleStats.description:
Engagement counts for an article, computed at read time. These are
Commune side counts, not provider side email metrics: opens, clicks and
deliveries are not here.

likes.description: How many people liked the article.

comments.description:
Replies in the article's chat thread. Commune has no separate
comments store: an article's discussion is a thread like any other,
so this counts the undeleted replies hanging off it. `0` when the
article has no thread.

ArticleStatus.title: ArticleStatus
ArticleStatus.description:
Where an article is in its life. A credential holding only `read`
permissions ever sees `sent` and nothing else. An imported article is
always `sent`, since Commune sees it after the provider delivered it.

Esp.title: Esp
Esp.description:
Where a newsletter is published from. `commune` means Commune itself
sends the email. Every other value is an email service provider whose
posts Commune imports. `rss` covers any feed that is not one of the
named providers.

Media.title: Media
Media.description: An image or file attached to a thread or a message.

url.description: Where the attachment is served from.

type.description:
The attachment's media type when Commune recorded one, for example
`image/png`. Null for an attachment old enough that none was
recorded.

thumbnail.description: A smaller rendition, when one was generated.

Newsletter.title: Newsletter
Newsletter.description:
A newsletter and its public profile. Nothing operational is exposed:
ESP credentials, OAuth tokens, group and audience ids, feed polling
state and language detection bookkeeping all stay server side.

handle.description:
The short, unique, URL safe name. Resolves the public profile at
`/n/{handle}` and is accepted anywhere `{newsletter}` is.

name.description: Display name, as the creator writes it.

description.description:
The profile blurb. Sanitised HTML, not plain text, because creators
format it. Treat it as untrusted markup and render it in a
sandboxed context.

website_url.description: The creator's own site, if they linked one.

language.description:
Best known language of the newsletter's writing as a BCP 47 tag.
Detected from recent articles rather than declared, so treat it as a
hint. Null before enough has been published to tell.

chat_create_permission.description: Who may start a new chat thread in this community.

allow_non_subscriber_chat.description:
Whether people who have not subscribed may reply in existing
threads.

owner.description:
The account that owns the newsletter. A `Ref` unless `owner` is
named in `?expand=`.

featured_article.description:
The article the creator pinned to the top of the profile, or `null`
when none is pinned. A `Ref` unless `featured_article` is named in
`?expand=`.

created_at.description: When the newsletter was connected to or created on Commune.

Ref.title: Ref
Ref.description:
An unexpanded relationship. Ask for the relationship in `?expand=` to
get the full object in its place.

object.description: The type of the referenced resource.

id.description:
The referenced resource's `id`, in whatever form that resource's own
schema declares. Most are UUIDs; a `Ref` whose `object` is `user`
carries an account identifier, which is an opaque string and not a
UUID. Compare it for equality and pass it back; do not parse it.

SocialLinks.title: SocialLinks
SocialLinks.description:
The creator's other homes on the internet, stored as canonical profile
URLs. Every key is optional and a newsletter that set none returns an
empty object.

mastodon.description: Mastodon profile URL, including the instance host.

Thread.title: Thread
Thread.description:
A conversation in a newsletter's community, together with the message
that opened it. Its replies are a separate collection.

short_id.description:
Eight character base62 identifier used by the thread's own URL at
`/n/{handle}/chat/{short_id}`. Null for a thread Commune opened
under an article, which is reached through the article instead.

newsletter.description:
The community this thread lives in. A `Ref` unless `newsletter` is
named in `?expand=`.

author.description:
Who opened the thread. A `Ref` unless `author` is named in
`?expand=`.

content.description:
The opening message. HTML, since people format what they write.
Treat it as untrusted markup and render it in a sandboxed context.

is_article_thread.description:
`true` when Commune opened this thread under an article rather than
a person starting it. These are kept off the global feed, because
the article card already represents the conversation there.

article.description:
The article that opened this thread, when `is_article_thread` is
`true`. `null` otherwise. A `Ref` unless `article` is named in
`?expand=`.

reply_count.description: Undeleted replies in the thread, at any depth.

view_count.description: How many times the thread was opened.

updated_at.description: When the thread row last changed for any reason.

edited_at.description:
When the author last edited the opening message. Null when it was
never edited, which is what drives the edited marker in the product.

last_activity_at.description:
When the thread last received a reply, or when it was opened if it
never did. This is the sort key for the thread list.

ThreadVisibility.title: ThreadVisibility
ThreadVisibility.description:
Where a thread is placed. `public` puts it on the global Commune feed
and makes it readable by anyone. `subscribers` keeps it inside the
newsletter. `paid` narrows it further to the paying part of the
audience. Set and changed by the newsletter's team.

User.title: User
User.description:
A person's public profile, and the whole of what this API returns about
anybody other than the credential's own owner. Email address, theme,
notification preferences, push subscriptions, read state and saved
articles are never carried.

username.description:
The unique handle the profile resolves on at `/@{username}`. Null
for an account that has not finished signing up.

display_name.description: The name shown next to their messages and bylines.

avatar.description:
Profile picture. Commune falls back to a generated avatar when the
person never set one, so this is rarely null in practice.
